items.description: after the add-and-backfill migration runs on a seeded stock row, that row exposes batch_number and serial_number as distinct, separately addressable columns
after the add-and-backfill migration, location and inventory_code remain present and unchanged on a seeded stock row
after a single-step downgrade followed by a single-step upgrade on the real branch database, the stock table has a batch_number column and a serial_number column
the API boundary module (app/routes/) imports only from the service layer and contains no SQLAlchemy session or ORM imports
the service module (app/services/) contains no SQLAlchemy session or ORM model imports; only the repository layer imports from the ORM
DATABASE_URL is read from the environment variable and is not hard-coded in any application module
after the migration, a stock row whose inventory_code was a hyphen-delimited location-batch-serial code has batch_number set to the second hyphen-delimited segment
after the migration, a stock row whose inventory_code was a hyphen-delimited location-batch-serial code has serial_number set to the third hyphen-delimited segment
after the migration, a stock row whose inventory_code has fewer than three hyphen-delimited segments has batch_number left NULL
after the migration, a stock row whose inventory_code has fewer than three hyphen-delimited segments has serial_number left NULL
after the migration, a nonconforming stock row is still present in the table with its sku unchanged
inserting a stock row with batch_number=NULL and serial_number=NULL against the real branch database succeeds without a constraint violation
inserting a stock row with sku=NULL against the real branch database raises a NOT NULL constraint violation
after the migration, the stock row count scoped to the test's own seeded rows is identical before and after the upgrade
after the migration, each seeded stock row retains its original sku value unchanged
after the migration, each seeded stock row retains its original location value unchanged
after the migration, each seeded stock row retains its original quantity value unchanged
inserting two stock rows with the same (sku, location) pair against the real branch database raises a UniqueViolation error

the migration upgrade (add batch_number and serial_number) and its backfill UPDATE execute inside a single transaction; injecting a failure mid-backfill leaves neither column nor any partial backfill on the real branch database
the count of test-owned stock rows on the real branch database is identical before and after the upgrade migration
for every stock row seeded before the upgrade migration, the sku, location, and quantity values are unchanged after the upgrade runs against the real branch database
when the integrity probe is run after backfill on a mixed table of conforming and nonconforming codes, it returns the exact count of rows whose batch_number and serial_number are both NULL
